source_title: Policy on Maximum Timer Interval and Exposure Schedule for Sunlamp Products; Appendix B melanogenesis action spectrum table
table_location: Appendix B, 'Parrish Melanogenesis Type II Skin (1982) Normalized to 292 nm', 1-nm table 250-405 nm
authors: Parrish JA, Jaenicke KF, Anderson RR (via FDA CDRH transcription)
identifier: DOI 10.1111/j.1751-1097.1982.tb04362.x; PMID 7122713 (original study); FDA Form 3630 Appendix B (distributable table)
biological_endpoint: delayed pigmentation (new melanogenesis, distinct from immediate pigment darkening). SunStack uses this as an action-spectrum-based exposure index; it is not a universal prediction of melanin production or visible future skin color.
subject_population: Type II skin (always burns, then tans slightly); small-n historical monochromator study, visual grading of delayed tanning ~7 days after exposure
wavelengths_tested_nm: 250-405 nm as transcribed (production domain 280-400); standard MMD = 459 J/m2 at 296 nm; standard MED = 156 J/m2 at 296 nm (erythema appendix)
assessment_time_after_exposure: delayed pigmentation assessed ~7 days after exposure (visual grading)
normalization_convention: 1.0 at 296 nm (table maximum; 'Normalized to 292 nm' is the table title, actual maximum value 1.0 sits at 296 nm)
original_units: dimensionless relative effectiveness Ji (reciprocal minimal melanogenesis dose); exposure time Tm = 1836 J/m2 / sum(Ji*Ri)
digitization_method: manual transcription of the Appendix B 1-nm printed table via pdftotext (pdfminer-equivalent layout extraction) + regex pair parsing, verified: 156 entries 250-405 nm contiguous, maximum 1.0 at 296 nm, self-consistent log-interpolated values (spot: 309 = 0.14087 == sqrt(308*310) to 5dp). Two print-layout repairs: '767007E.03' read as 0.767007E-03 (row 363); 292 '.8874598' kept verbatim (consistent with log-neighbors). PDF saved alongside provenance tooling, not in repo.
transcription_provenance: transcribed 2026-09-30 from FDA-3630_Stat_Sec_Ext_09-23-2026.pdf (1436249 bytes, served as attachment filename FDA-3630_Stat_Sec_Ext_09-23-2026.pdf)
anchor_points: none - the table is already 1-nm; no anchor interpolation is used in production
interpolation_guidance: no interpolation needed within the 1-nm production grid; outside 280-400 nm the loader domain gate applies. Log-space interpolation remains the selected reconstruction method only where resampling is unavoidable; linear-effectiveness interpolation is not the selected method and is inappropriate for this reconstruction because effectiveness spans orders of magnitude unless independently validated.
license_distribution_note: US federal government publication (FDA), publicly downloadable without authentication; reproduced wavelength/effectiveness values with full provenance. Not legal advice; re-verify distribution terms before commercial redistribution.
uncertainty_note: Historical small-panel visual-grading study on Type II skin; printed-table precision (5-6 significant digits) is transcription fidelity, not measurement uncertainty. Values below ~300 nm and above ~390 nm carry larger underlying uncertainty. No per-wavelength uncertainty published in the table.
limitations: Type II skin only; small historical subject panel; visual grading; not a universal melanin-production predictor. Replaces the 280-289 nm unity assumption of action-spectrum-v1 (measured table: 280 nm = 0.314, not 1.0).
